Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority,

to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
ROUND LEATHER BELTING FOR SMALL MACHINES 

( First Revision ) 



1- Scope — Covers the requirements of round leather belting of the ' smooth type ', for small drives. 



2. Term 

of terms 
shall apply. 



inology — For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given In IS : 1640-1960 ' Glossary 
relating to hides, skin and leather' and 15:2954-1964 * Vegetable tanned leather for belting '

3.1 The thickness and width shall be measured at least at 10 places, 3 m apart, of a spool and the 
average recorded. 

4. Material — The leather for the manufacture of the belting shall conform to IS : 2954-1964. 

5. Manufacture 

5.1 Sfr/ps — Strips shall be cut from bends, except that the bend shall be straightened by removing 
a strip along the backbone as illustrated In Fig. 1. 



THIN REGION 




>4BCD — belting butt bend 

vAiBiCiDj — thin region about the backbone which may have to be rejected if too thin (in 
buffalo hides ) 

FIG. 1 METHOD OF CUTTING STRIP FROM BENDS 

5.2 The butts shall be made into round belts either by hand or by machines. 

5.3 The belts shall be compact and shall have a smooth finish free from small hair or hair roots.

6. Tests 



6.1 Breaking Strength •— The minimum breaking strength for the various sizes of belts, determined in 
accordance with the method given in 18:5914-1970 ' Methods of physical testing of leather', shall 
be as given below: 



Nominal Size 

mm 


iMinimum Breaicing 

Strength 

N 


5 (Heavy) 

6 (Regular) 

7 ( Heavy ) 


441 
667 
755 



6-2 E/ongai/on — The elongation of the belt, determined in the manner described In 18:5914-1970 
shall be not more than 6 percent when a load of 520 N/cm^ cross-section is applied for 15 minutes. 
The permanent elongation, after the load has been removed and the belt allowed to hang unloaded 
for four hours, shall not exceed 2 percent. 

6.3 Cracking — The leather shall not crack when the belt is bent through an angle of 180 degrees, 
grain side out, around a mandrel of 25 mm diameter. 

7. Packing and Marking 

7.1 The belting shall be paclced as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. The number 
of pieces per spool of 30 m shall not be more than four. No piece shall be shorter than 2 m In 
length. 

7.2 The packages shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer or his recognized trade-mark, 
if any; number of pieces in the package; and the month and year of manufacture. 

7.3 ISI Certification A/farA/V?sf — Details available with the Indian 8tandards Institution. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first issued in 1962. In the present revision the requirements pertaining to 
the leather for belting have been deleted and reference has been made to 18 : 2954-1 964 ' Vegetable 
tanned leather for belting '. The values specified In the standard have been given in 81 units.
